title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: set how long policy matches are retained
summary: The roadmap facts, portal controls, licensing and preservation behaviour are supported. The briefing correctly distinguishes the planned change from the setting already documented in Learn. Remove the unsupported assertion that no reviewer approves deletion; Microsoft documents automatic deletion but does not explicitly describe an approval mechanism.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans the ability to define how long content captured by a Communication Compliance policy is retained.
claims.quote: Introducing the ability to define how long content captured by a Communication Compliance policy is retained.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn documents Policy Match Preservation as a Communication Compliance portal setting.
claims.quote: Select the Settings button in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Communication Compliance to go to the Communication Compliance global settings. Select the Policy Match Preservation setting, then select a new time period.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Communication Compliance stores a copy, not the original, when a policy finds a matching message.
claims.quote: When a Communication Compliance policy finds a message that matches the policy, the solution stores a copy of the message (not the original message).

claims.claim: Learn says the preservation setting can be used starting June 1, 2025, rather than waiting for the roadmap's 2027 target.
claims.quote: Starting June 1, 2025, you can use the Policy Match Preservation setting to specify how long to save policy matches in Communication Compliance.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The documented preservation-period options are 1 month, 6 months, 1 year and 7 years.
claims.quote: You can choose 1 month, 6 months, 1 year, or 7 years.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Learn-documented global preservation setting defaults to 1 year.
claims.quote: The default value is 1 year.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A preservation period selected within a policy takes precedence over the global setting.
claims.quote: You can also specify a preservation period when you create or edit a policy. The preservation period you select within a policy takes precedence over the global Policy Match Preservation setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The system automatically deletes policy matches older than the selected preservation period.
claims.quote: The system automatically deletes policy matches that are older than the selected time period.

claims.claim: Deletion of expired policy matches is permanent.
claims.quote: For example, if the Policy Match Preservation setting is 1 year (the default), the system permanently deletes any policy matches older than 1 year as of September 1.

claims.claim: Preservation deletion removes Communication Compliance copies, not originals in user shards.
claims.quote: Only the policy matches in Communication Compliance are deleted because they're copies of the original messages. This process doesn't delete original copies from user shards.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management can set a retention policy for the original messages.
claims.quote: You can use Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management to set up a retention policy for original messages.

claims.claim: The channel-signals page still says copies used for analysis and investigation remain for as long as the policy is in place.
claims.quote: Communication Compliance policies retain copies of messages used for analysis and investigation for as long as a policy is in place, even if users leave your organization and their mailboxes are deleted.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changes to the global preservation period apply going forward.
claims.quote: If you change the time period in the setting after September 1, the preservation period applies going forward.

claims.claim: Previously stamped policy matches keep their earlier preservation period when the global period changes.
claims.quote: if you select 1 year as the time period on September 1, then change the setting to 7 years on September 3, policy matches from September 1 and September 2 are preserved for 1 year, and policy matches starting on September 3 are preserved for 7 years.

The policies page says PowerShell is not supported for creating and managing Communication Compliance policies.
